class="section"><div class="desc"><h3><a href="../../../Projects/Libraries-and-Frameworks/Theia-ECS/theia-rewrite" class="internal">Theia Complete Rewrite: Benchmark Results Sneak Peek</a></h3></div><p class="meta"><time datetime="2026-04-09T03:00:00.000Z">Apr 09, 2026</time></p><ul class="tags"></ul></div></li></ul></div></div><div class="center"><div class="page-header"><div class="popover-hint"><p show-comma="true" class="content-meta"><time datetime="2026-04-26T03:00:00.000Z">Apr 26, 2026</time><span>3 min read</span></p><nav class="breadcrumb-container" aria-label="breadcrumbs"><div class="breadcrumb-element"><a href="../../../">Home</a><p> ❯ </p></div><div class="breadcrumb-element"><a href="../../../Projects/">Projects</a><p> ❯ </p></div><div href="../../../Projects/Libraries-and-Frameworks/Theia-ECS/">Theia ECS</a><p> ❯ </p></div><div class="breadcrumb-element"><a href>Theia Rewrite: Updated Benchmark Results</a></div></nav><h1 class="article-title">Theia Rewrite: Updated Benchmark Results</h1></div></div><article class="popover-hint"><h3 id="its-done-almost">It’s Done! (Almost)<a role="anchor" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1" data-no-popover="true" href="#its-done-almost" class="internal"><svg width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M10 13a5 5 0 0 0 7.54.54l3-3a5 5 0 0 0-7.07-7.07l-1.72 1.71"></path><path d="M14 11a5 5 0 0 0-7.54-.54l-3 3a5 5 0 0 0 7.07 7.07l1.71-1.71"></path></svg></a></h3>
<p>It’s been almost <strong>two months</strong> since I decided to <strong>develop the entire framework from scratch</strong> again, and here we are, <strong>the job is done</strong>! Theia ECS is completely renewed and comes with <strong>even more features than before</strong>:</p>
<ul>
<li>Validation and strict constraints to ensure the use of <strong>only blittable types</strong>;</li>
<li><strong>Events</strong> (entity lifecycle, components, and relations), allowing different event scopes (World or Assemblage);</li>
<li><strong>Jobs</strong>, with <strong>built-in parallel</strong> systems and parallel query execution (per <em>chunk</em>);</li>
<li><strong>Types as enums</strong> (capable of matching or including a certain component or relation to an enum value);</li>
<li><strong>World-bounded</strong> single-instance components, known as <strong>singleton components</strong> (called Uniques);</li>
<li>Improved DataTable, now called ManagedData (a custom, dictionary-like collection for classes);</li>
<li>A <strong>greatly improved relation system</strong>: <span class="text-highlight">bilateral linkage, with all operations as O(1) and thread-safe</span>;</li>
<li>Improved Systems;</li>
<li>A greatly <strong>improved serialization/deserialization system</strong>;</li>
<li>Exceptions (yes, that is a feature!) screaming at the programmer so we don’t mess things up; for example, it <strong>throws when attempting to perform an action that may trigger a structural change during a query</strong>.</li>
</ul>
<p>Other basic features have also been improved, and <em>we’ll go over everything in detail another day</em>.</p>
<p>This new version <strong>greatly improves what I started around one or two years ago</strong>, and now, to be totally fair, <em>I feel ashamed of a lot of the mistakes made in the old version</em>… but just like our <em>for loops</em>, <span class="text-highlight">we need to iterate on our solutions in order to improve our work</span>.</p>
<p>As I pointed out in the <a href="../../../Projects/Libraries-and-Frameworks/Theia-ECS/theia-rewrite" class="internal alias" data-slug="Projects/Libraries-and-Frameworks/Theia-ECS/theia-rewrite">sneak peek</a> article, <span class="text-highlight">Theia’s new version is fully implemented in managed C#</span> (that means no unsafe code), and now, with version 1.0 finished and <strong>updated benchmark results</strong>, I can safely say that <span class="text-highlight">Theia is one of the fastest C# ECS framework (usually scoring #1 in most counts across many different categories, according to the presented benchmark) for the operations that matter most in a running game loop</span>: iterating entities via queries (it got even faster after a refactor I did since the sneak peek article), spawning and despawning, and relation management.</p>
<p>Just to refresh our memories, due to its archetype’s underlying implementation, which aims for lazy initialization of chunks, structural changes when adding or removing components can be a little costly at high entity counts, as I mentioned before.</p>
<p>Without further ado, as I did in the sneak peek, I’ve decided to compile all the results and plot them on a graph. <strong>Check out the results for yourself below!</strong> Theia’s new version will be <strong>released soon</strong>, including the benchmark (with the results) and unit test projects; the <strong>final step is solid documentation</strong>, which is already on the way!</p>

      [19.24],[13.79],[10.00],[16.20],[17.83],[75.61]]}

const state = {
  catIdx: 0,
  variantIdx: 0,
  hidden: new Set()
};

let chart = null;

function getCat(){return CATS[state.catIdx];}
function getVariant(){return getCat().variants[state.variantIdx];}
function isSkipped(fwIdx){
  const skip = getCat().skip || [];
  return skip.includes(fwIdx);
}

function renderCats(){
  const el = document.getElementById('cats');
  el.innerHTML = '';
  CATS.forEach((cat, i) => {
    if (i === 12) {
      const d1 = document.createElement('span');
      d1.className = 'divider';
      el.appendChild(d1);
    }
    if (i === 20) {
      const d2 = document.createElement('span');
      d2.className = 'divider';
      el.appendChild(d2);
    }
    const b = document.createElement('button');
    b.className = 'cat' + (i === state.catIdx ? ' on' : '');
    b.textContent = cat.label;
    b.addEventListener('click', () => selectCat(i));
    el.appendChild(b);
  });
}

function renderTabs(){
  const cat = getCat();
  const tvars = document.getElementById('tvars');
  if (cat.noTabs) {
    tvars.style.display = 'none';
    return;
  }
  tvars.style.display = 'flex';
  const btns = tvars.querySelectorAll('.tv');
  const variantNames = cat.variants.map(v => v.name);
  btns.forEach((b, i) => {
    const tabName = ['T1','T3','T5'][i];
    let targetVariantName = tabName;
    if (cat.label === 'Remove component' && i === 0) targetVariantName = 'T2';
    const idx = variantNames.indexOf(targetVariantName);
    const enabled = idx !== -1;
    b.disabled = !enabled;
    b.classList.toggle('on', enabled && idx === state.variantIdx);
    b.textContent = (cat.label === 'Remove component' && i === 0) ? 'T2' : tabName;
    b.onclick = enabled ? () => selectVariant(idx) : null;
  });
  document.getElementById('sub').textContent = getVariant().sub;
}

function renderLegend(){
  const el = document.getElementById('leg');
  el.innerHTML = '';
  FW.forEach((f, i) => {
    const b = document.createElement('button');
    const skipped = isSkipped(i);
    b.className = 'li' + (skipped ? ' na' : (state.hidden.has(i) ? ' off' : ''));
    b.disabled = skipped;
    b.innerHTML = `<span class="ld" style="background:${f.c}"></span>${f.n}`;
    if (!skipped) {
      b.addEventListener('click', () => toggleFw(i));
    }
    el.appendChild(b);
  });
}

function toggleFw(i){
  if (state.hidden.has(i)) state.hidden.delete(i);
  else state.hidden.add(i);
  renderLegend();
  renderChart();
}

function selectCat(i){
  state.catIdx = i;
  state.hidden = new Set();
  const cat = getCat();
  if (cat.noTabs) {
    state.variantIdx = 0;
  } else {
    state.variantIdx = 0;
  }
  renderCats();
  renderTabs();
  renderLegend();
  renderChart();
  document.getElementById('ins').textContent = getVariant().ins;
}

function selectVariant(i){
  state.variantIdx = i;
  renderTabs();
  renderChart();
  document.getElementById('ins').textContent = getVariant().ins;
}

function renderChart(){
  const cat = getCat();
  const variant = getVariant();
  const labels = cat.rel ? RELATION_LABELS : (cat.bar ? [''] : ENTITY_LABELS);
  const chartType = cat.bar ? 'bar' : 'line';

  const datasets = variant.rows.map((row, i) => {
    if (row === null) return null;
    if (state.hidden.has(i)) return null;
    if (chartType === 'bar') {
      return {
        label: FW[i].n,
        data: row,
        backgroundColor: FW[i].c,
        borderColor: FW[i].c,
        borderWidth: 0
      };
    }
    return {
      label: FW[i].n,
      data: row,
      borderColor: FW[i].c,
      backgroundColor: FW[i].c + '22',
      borderWidth: i === 0 ? 2.5 : 1.5,
      pointRadius: i === 0 ? 4 : 2.5,
      spanGaps: true,
      tension: 0.3,
      fill: false,
      borderDash: i === 0 ? [] : [4,3]
    };
  }).filter(Boolean);

  const isDark = matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches;
  const gridColor = isDark ? 'rgba(255,255,255,0.07)' : 'rgba(0,0,0,0.06)';
  const tickColor = isDark ? '#999' : '#666';

  if (chart) {
    chart.destroy();
    chart = null;
  }
  const canvas = document.getElementById('ch');
  chart = new Chart(canvas, {
    type: chartType,
    data: { labels, datasets },
    options: {
      responsive: true,
      maintainAspectRatio: false,
      animation: false,
      plugins: {
        legend: { display: false },
        tooltip: {
          callbacks: {
            label: c => ` ${c.dataset.label}: ${c.parsed.y != null ? c.parsed.y.toFixed(2) + ' μs' : 'N/A'}`
          }
        }
      },
      scales: {
        x: { grid: { color: gridColor }, ticks: { color: tickColor, font: { size: 11 } } },
        y: {
          grid: { color: gridColor },
          ticks: {
            color: tickColor,
            font: { size: 11 },
            callback: v => v >= 1000 ? (v/1000).toFixed(1) + 'ms' : v + 'μs'
          }
        }
      }
    }
  });
}

renderCats();
renderTabs();
renderLegend();
renderChart();
document.getElementById('ins').textContent = getVariant().ins;
</script>

</article>
